situation: A relative at a family function asks, "So, when are you getting married?"
say: Haha, see, uncle... let's see, whatever is written in destiny will happen.
better: Not right now, uncle. I'm focusing on work this year. How's Rohan doing in Pune?
also: When it happens, you'll be the first to know. Tell me, how is your knee now?
weak: Why do you people always ask this? It's my life.
Uncle, please, not again, I'm going to cry.
why: Answer briefly and kindly, then change the topic. No need to defend or explain.

situation: Your parents keep sending you marriage profiles after you have asked them to wait.
say: Mummy, I told you na, don't send all this, I'm not interested only.
better: Ma, I know you mean well. I'm not ready to look yet. Can we talk about it again after Diwali?
also: Please stop sending profiles for now. I'll tell you myself when I'm ready.
weak: Okay okay, send, I will see later.
You never listen to me, so why should I listen to you?
why: Shows you understand their care, then sets a clear limit and a time to revisit.

situation: Your father compares you to your cousin who got a job abroad.
say: Then go and adopt Ankit only, why do you need me?
better: I'm happy for Ankit. I'm on a different path, and I'd like you to judge me on my own progress.
also: Comparing us hurts, Papa. Ask me how my work is going instead.
weak: Fine, I'm useless, happy now?
Ankit is not that great also, you don't know the full story.
why: Names the hurt without attacking anyone, and asks for what you actually want.

situation: You want to tell your parents you are leaving engineering to study design.
say: Papa, actually, I was just thinking, maybe, if you don't mind, I may change my course...
better: Papa, I've decided to switch to design. I've thought it through, and I'd like to show you my plan.
also: I want to talk about my course. I've made a plan and I'd like your support.
weak: I'm leaving engineering, end of discussion.
Sorry, sorry, I know you'll be angry, I'm a failure.
why: State the decision plainly and come prepared. Hedging invites them to talk you out of it.

situation: An aunt asks how much salary you get at your new job.
say: Aunty, it's okay, not much, just adjusting somehow.
better: It's a good package, aunty, I'm happy with it. The work is really interesting too.
also: I keep salary between me and my parents, aunty. But the job is going well.
weak: Why do you want to know, aunty?
Fourteen lakh, plus bonus, plus ESOPs, plus health cover.
why: You don't owe anyone a number. A warm, short answer closes the topic.

situation: Your mother asks you to come home every weekend, but you need rest.
say: Mummy, I'll try, let's see, I'm very busy only.
better: I can't come every weekend, Ma, I need some rest too. I'll come on the last weekend of every month.
also: Let's do a video call every Sunday, and I'll visit once a month.
weak: You don't understand how tiring my life is.
Okay, I'll come, no problem. (and then doesn't go)
why: A clear, honest promise is kinder than a vague 'I'll try' that you break.

situation: Your parents criticise your partner, whom they have met only once.
say: You people are always like this, you hate everyone I like.
better: I know you've only met Kavya once. Give her a real chance. Let's have dinner together next week.
also: I'd like you to know her before deciding. What exactly worries you?
weak: Fine, I'll marry whoever you want, happy?
She's better than all of you anyway.
why: Asks for fairness and a next step instead of turning it into a war.

situation: A relative says you have put on weight since the last wedding.
say: Haha, yes aunty, too much eating, what to do.
better: I'd rather not talk about my weight, aunty. Tell me, how was your trip to Shirdi?
also: I'm feeling good, aunty, that's what matters to me.
weak: You've also become quite fat, aunty.
Yes, I know, I hate how I look, I'm trying.
why: Quietly declines the topic and moves on. No insult back, no self-blame.

situation: Your parents ask when you'll take a 'proper government job' instead of your startup.
say: Government job is for boring people, I don't want to rot there.
better: I understand you want me to be secure. Here's my savings plan if the startup doesn't work out.
also: Give me two years. If it isn't working by then, I'll look for a stable job.
weak: You won't understand startups, Papa.
Yes, yes, I'll prepare for UPSC from next month.
why: Speaks to their real fear, security, and gives a concrete plan and time limit.

situation: Your sibling borrowed your laptop and returned it with a cracked screen.
say: You always spoil my things, you're so careless, I'm telling Mummy.
better: The screen is cracked. The repair will cost about six thousand. Can you share the cost?
also: I'm upset about the screen. Next time, ask me before taking it out of the house.
weak: It's fine, leave it, I'll manage. (and sulks for a week)
Never touch my things again in your life.
why: Describe the problem and ask for a fix. Skip 'always' and blaming the person.

situation: Your parents want you to attend a long puja on the day of your exam.
say: I can't come, I have exam, you people don't care about my studies.
better: I have an exam that day, so I'll miss the puja. I'll come in the evening and touch everyone's feet.
also: Can I join for the aarti after my exam? I don't want to miss it fully.
weak: Puja is more important than my exam, is it?
I'll see, maybe I'll come, maybe not.
why: States the clash plainly and offers what you can do, so no one feels dismissed.

situation: You need to tell your parents you are moving to another city for a job.
say: Papa, so... there is one small thing... don't get angry, okay?
better: Papa, I've got a job offer in Bengaluru and I've accepted it. Can we talk about how we'll stay in touch?
also: I have news: I'm moving to Bengaluru next month. I'd like your blessing.
weak: I'm going, whether you like it or not.
Maybe I'll move, maybe not, nothing is final, chill.
why: Lead with the news itself. A nervous build-up makes people expect bad news.

situation: A relative gives unasked advice about how you should raise your child.
say: Aunty, in our time things are different, you won't understand.
better: Thanks, aunty. We've spoken to our doctor and we're happy with how we're doing it.
also: I'll keep that in mind. We've found what works for us.
weak: Please mind your own business.
Oh, you're right, we're doing everything wrong.
why: Thank them, then make clear the decision is yours. Polite and final.

situation: Your mother asks if you have eaten, for the fourth time today.
say: Haan haan, I ate, why do you keep asking, so irritating.
better: Yes, Ma, I had dal-chawal at two. I'm fine, don't worry.
also: I ate well, Ma. I'll send you a photo of dinner tonight.
weak: Stop treating me like a baby.
Hmm.
why: A specific answer calms worry faster than an annoyed one. It's love, not checking.

situation: You want to apologise to your father after an angry argument last night.
say: Papa, chai? (and act like nothing happened)
better: Papa, I'm sorry I raised my voice last night. I still disagree, but I shouldn't have spoken like that.
also: I was rude yesterday, and I'm sorry. Can we talk calmly tonight?
weak: Sorry if you felt bad.
Okay sorry, but you also started it.
why: Apologise for how you spoke without giving up your view. No 'if' or 'but'.

situation: Relatives ask why you and your spouse don't have children yet.
say: Haha, planning is going on, aunty, you'll get good news soon.
better: That's something we keep between the two of us, aunty. Have you tried the gulab jamun?
also: We're happy as we are right now. Thanks for asking.
weak: That's none of your business.
We're trying, but there are some medical issues, actually...
why: Private topics can stay private. A calm line and a topic change are enough.

situation: Your parents disapprove of you living with flatmates of the opposite gender.
say: It's normal nowadays, you are so backward, everybody does it.
better: I understand it feels new to you. They're colleagues, the flat is safe, and you're welcome to visit and meet them.
also: What worries you most? Let me answer that honestly.
weak: I'll lie to them, it's easier.
It's my life, I don't have to explain anything.
why: Calling parents 'backward' ends the talk. Inviting them in builds trust.

situation: Your brother asks you to lend him money again, though he hasn't repaid the last loan.
say: Bhai, actually, my hand is a little tight this month, sorry yaar.
better: I can't lend more until the last twenty thousand comes back. If you're in real trouble, let's sit and look at it together.
also: I won't lend this time. I'm happy to help you make a budget, though.
weak: Okay, how much? (and resents it)
You're useless with money, everyone knows.
why: An honest reason and a real offer of help is better than a fake excuse.

situation: Your parents keep asking about your job search, and you feel stressed.
say: Stop asking every day! I'm trying na, what else do you want?
better: I know you're worried. Daily questions make me more anxious. I'll update you every Sunday, I promise.
also: I've applied to twelve places and have two interviews. I'll tell you when there's news.
weak: Nothing is happening, I'm a failure, okay?
Everything is fine, don't worry. (when it isn't)
why: Explains how the questions feel and gives them a regular update instead.

situation: Your in-laws visit and rearrange your kitchen without asking.
say: Mummyji, it's okay, whatever you like. (and silently fumes)
better: Thank you for helping, Mummyji. I've kept things this way so I can find them quickly, so I'll put them back.
also: I'd love your help with cooking tonight. Let's keep the kitchen setup as it is, though.
weak: Please don't touch my things in my house.
Your son also never puts anything back, it runs in the family.
why: Thanks the intent and keeps your limit. Being polite doesn't mean saying nothing.

situation: Your parents ask you to drop your partner because they are from another community.
say: Then I'll run away and marry, you can't stop me.
better: I love you both, and I love her. I'm asking you to meet her family once before you decide.
also: I know this is hard for you. I'm not changing my mind, but I want you with me.
weak: Okay, I'll leave her. (and doesn't)
You are all bigots.
why: Firm about your choice, gentle with them. Threats harden people; meeting softens them.

situation: Your grandmother asks you to explain UPI payments again.
say: Dadi, I already told you three times, it's so simple only.
better: Let's do it together, Dadi. You press the buttons and I'll guide you. I'll write the steps on a card too.
also: No problem, Dadi. Let's send ten rupees to me as practice.
weak: Leave it, give me the phone, I'll do it.
Ask Bunty, I'm busy.
why: Patience and doing it with her teaches better than repeating it louder.

situation: Your father says you wasted money on a trip with friends.
say: It's my money, I earned it, I'll spend how I want.
better: It was my savings, Papa, and I'd planned for it. I still put aside my monthly investment, so we're fine.
also: I needed the break. My budget is on track. Want to see it?
weak: Sorry, I won't go anywhere again.
You also waste money on your cricket kit.
why: Calmly shows you were responsible. Facts answer worry better than defiance.

situation: Your cousin asks you to pretend she's at your house so she can go to a party.
say: Okay fine, but if Chachi finds out I don't know anything.
better: I'm not comfortable lying to Chachi. If you want, I'll help you ask her properly.
also: I won't cover for you, but I'll back you up when you tell her the truth.
weak: Are you mad? I'm telling Chachi right now.
Hmm, let me think, I'll tell you later.
why: Says no to the lie but stays on her side. Clear, not preachy.

situation: Your mother forwards a fake health message in the family WhatsApp group.
say: Mummy, this is all fake, don't forward such nonsense.
better: Ma, I checked this one and it isn't true. Doctors say the opposite. Here's a link from AIIMS.
also: Before forwarding health tips, send them to me first and I'll check them.
weak: Uncle, aunty, everyone please stop being so dumb.
(leaves the group)
why: Correct the message, not the person, and show a trustworthy source.
